content.text:
Interesting! The JS render work is only 2.6ms per frame, yet FPS is 2-7. That means the bottleneck is rasterization/compositing by the browser, not JS. Canvas drawing commands are queued and rasterized asynchronously; JS time doesn't include GPU/software rasterization flush. So drawing 4 full-screen layers is indeed fill-rate. The canvas rasterization at 1280x800 with SwiftShader is slow. A real GPU handles it.

Can we reduce fill cost? The `render` does:
- clearRect full canvas
- fill world gradient (full screen)
- draw zone image (full screen, scaled)
- puddles etc.
- atmosphere full-screen fill
- vignette full-screen radial gradient.

If we pre-composite the gradient + zone art into one image and pre-render atmosphere/vignette into one overlay image, the browser still has to rasterize:
- zone art image full screen (1 pass)
- overlay image full screen (1 pass)
Current: under fill + zone art + atmosphere fill + vignette fill = 4 passes. Combining could cut to 2. That should roughly double FPS. On real GPU already 60. Nice.

Can we eliminate overlay passes altogether? Use CSS `#atmosphere` and `#vignette` fixed divs with CSS gradients; GPU compositing might be much faster in hardware, but with SwiftShader still full-screen rasterization once per frame? CSS layers are cached; if static, compositor can reuse them, potentially free. The vignette static; atmosphere static per zone. For hurt flash and low HP pulse, use another layer with opacity. This could dramatically improve FPS even in software if cached as composited layers. However, browsers may still composite. CSS opacity changes on a cached layer is cheap.

But architecture change is more work. Simpler: pre-render the "under + zone art" into one canvas per zone at load (world width x height at S maybe 0.8) and remove the separate under gradient. Then each frame draw just the zone art once. And pre-render atmosphere+vignette into a screen-sized overlay stored on resize/zone change, draw once. Two draws vs four. In SwiftShader, still 2 full-screen draws, maybe 2x FPS. Good enough. But adding a screen-size overlay updated on zone change: zone changes infrequent. Hurt flash dynamic: keep a separate dynamic flash (full-screen radial only when hurt, not most frames). Low HP pulse also only when low. So static overlay can include atmosphere+vignette base. Then dynamic hurt/low HP drawn only when active.

But a screen-sized overlay of a radial gradient needs re-render on resize. We can create it lazily in drawVignette/drawAtmosphere? Use an offscreen canvas `overlayArt` with key w,h,zone. Each frame `ctx.drawImage(overlayArt,0,0)`. Compose both atmosphere and base vignette into it on creation. That replaces 2 fills with 1 draw. Combined with merging under+zone art, 4→2.

Merging under+zone art:
- Current `under` is a linear gradient across the whole world, in world coords; then each zone art canvas (which has paper background) covers it. Since zone art has opaque paper fill, the under gradient is only visible at seams (feathered?)
